title: Air-gapped offline bundle signing + verification for Private backup/restore toolkit
creator: Connor O'Brien
content:
## Context
Private (on-prem / air-gapped) customers need a supported way to validate that the backup/restore toolkit bundle they receive is authentic and untampered, without relying on any external network calls. This ticket covers:
- Signing the offline bundle during release
- Shipping verification materials (signatures + checksums + key/cert chain as applicable)
- Adding deterministic, documented verification steps that Support/SE can safely recommend

Drivers:
- MedData Systems: on-prem / restricted egress, requires offline verification and evidence artifacts for change control
- FinBank: wants explicit DR readiness commitments and repeatable validation steps

## Scope
### In scope
- Define the signing + verification mechanism for the on-prem/air-gapped backup/restore bundle produced by Release Engineering
- Integrate signing into CI/release pipeline (fail closed)
- Provide an operator-facing verification flow:
  - Offline signature verification
  - Offline checksum verification
  - Clear error messages and remediation steps
- Document key distribution/rotation expectations and compatibility guarantees
- Provide minimal evidence artifacts suitable for customer change control (e.g., checksum manifest + signature file + release metadata)

### Out of scope
- Keyless/online verification flows requiring OIDC / Rekor transparency log lookups at verify time
- Full supply-chain attestation framework (SLSA provenance) beyond what we can ship offline in this release (we can add a follow-up)
- Signing customer-generated backups (this ticket is about signing Redwood-distributed bundles)

## Proposed approach (current working plan)
- Bundle artifact: `redwood-private-backup-restore-bundle_<version>_<platform>.tar.gz`
- Generate `SHA256SUMS` for all files in the bundle and ship alongside:
  - `SHA256SUMS`
  - `SHA256SUMS.sig` (detached signature)
  - `RELEASE.json` (human + machine readable release metadata: version, git sha, build timestamp, signing key id)
- Signing mechanism (pending final decision after Security review):
  - Option A (preferred for offline): GPG detached signature using Redwood Release key stored in HSM-backed CI secret store
  - Option B: cosign with an offline public key (no transparency log dependency at verify time)

Verification steps (offline):
1) Verify signature over checksum manifest
2) Verify checksums over bundle contents
3) (Optional) `redwood-private-installer bundle verify --bundle <path>` wrapper to reduce operator error

## Security considerations
Threat model: attacker can tamper with the bundle while it is in transit or stored on a staging file server / USB media. Operator must be able to detect tampering offline.
- We assume CI/build environment is trusted for this release; follow-up to add stronger provenance later.
- Keys:
  - Private signing key never leaves CI secret boundary (ideally HSM-backed or KMS-wrapped)
  - Public key distribution via Redwood docs + included in bundle as `redwood-release-public-key.asc` (with fingerprint pinned in docs)
- Rotation:
  - Maintain a keyring of active + previous public keys for >= 2 releases
  - Verification tooling should accept both current and previous keys during overlap window

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Release pipeline produces signed bundle artifacts for on-prem/air-gapped deliverable
- [ ] Verification can be performed on a machine with no outbound network access
- [ ] Docs include exact commands and expected outputs for verification (and common failure cases)
- [ ] Support-approved guidance: Support can instruct customers how to verify without asking for sensitive environment access
- [ ] CI gates:
  - Missing signature/checksum artifacts fails the release
  - Signature verification is validated as part of pipeline (self-check)
- [ ] Key fingerprint is documented and versioned; rotation plan reviewed by Security

## Implementation tasks
1) Decision + review
- Confirm signing mechanism (GPG vs cosign offline key) with Security (Marcus Lin) and Secrets/KMS (Hanae Suzuki)
- Document decision in release notes / internal ADR addendum (or link to packaging doc)

2) CI/release changes (Sahana Iyer + Connor O'Brien)
- Add signing step to bundle build job
- Store signing key material in release CI secrets (access controlled, audited)
- Produce artifacts: `SHA256SUMS`, detached signature, `RELEASE.json`, public key
- Add pipeline self-verification step

3) Installer/tooling (if needed)
- Add helper command (optional but strongly recommended): `bundle verify` that executes offline verification steps and prints a single PASS/FAIL report
- Ensure command does not attempt any network calls

4) Docs
- Update on-prem packaging doc: bundle layout, signature verification, checksum verification, key fingerprint pinning
- Add troubleshooting section: time skew, line endings, wrong key, corrupted downloads

## Open questions
- Do we want GPG (ubiquitous but easy to misuse) vs cosign offline key (clean UX but adds dependency)?
- Where do we publish the canonical public key and fingerprint?
  - Option: docs site + also ship inside bundle; fingerprint pinned in both
- How do we handle Windows verification instructions (some on-prem teams are Windows-first)?

## Notes / links
- Related packaging doc (Confluence): `sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/backup-bundle-layout-and-signing.json`
- Related release checklist (Drive): `sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/backup-restore-release-checklist.json`
- Related incidents: INT-631 (CI signing step fails for airgapped bundle)

## Stakeholders
- Release Engineering: Connor O'Brien (owner), Sahana Iyer (CI)
- Security: Marcus Lin (review), Hanae Suzuki (KMS/keys)
- Private Deployments: Vivek Kulkarni (requirements), Fatima Noor (on-prem validation)

## Rollout plan
- Ship as part of `private-installer-2025.03` bundle deliverable
- Validate on a completely offline VM image as part of pre-release checklist
- Provide a one-page customer handout snippet for SEs to include in MAPs
comments: 2025-02-03 (Marcus Lin): We need an explicit statement that verification is offline and does not require Rekor / external transparency logs at verify time. If cosign is used, it must be the offline public-key mode. Also document key rotation overlap and where the canonical fingerprint is published.

2025-02-05 (Connor O'Brien): Release side can support either GPG or cosign. GPG likely simplest for air-gapped customer tooling, but we need to be careful with how we distribute and pin the public key fingerprint. Suggest shipping the public key in the bundle and pinning fingerprint in docs + RELEASE.json.

2025-02-07 (Hanae Suzuki): Prefer a single release signing key rather than per-service keys for now. We can store the private key encrypted with KMS and restrict decrypt permissions to the release job role. Add audit log visibility for key use.

2025-02-12 (Fatima Noor): Please include a copy/paste verification section that works on minimal Linux installs. Customers sometimes only have busybox/coreutils; avoid requiring too many extra packages. Also note that they may transfer bundles via USB, so checksum verification must be very explicit.

2025-02-18 (Sahana Iyer): Implemented pipeline self-check step in staging: build -> sign SHA256SUMS -> verify signature -> verify checksums. Still deciding whether to add an installer wrapper command or keep it docs-only. Leaning to add `bundle verify` to reduce operator error.
